function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

Here’s a quick rundown of the most common “tools” (websites, apps, APIs, and platforms) you can use to book flights:

| Category | Tool / Service | What it offers | Typical use‑case |
|----------|----------------|----------------|------------------|
| **Online Travel Agencies (OTAs)** | **Expedia** | Aggregates flights, hotels, car rentals, packages. | One‑stop booking for multi‑service trips. |
| | **Kayak** | Flight comparison engine, price alerts, flexible date search. | Finding the cheapest or best‑value flight. |
| | **Skyscanner** | Global flight search, price alerts, multi‑city itineraries. | Great for exploring destinations and dates. |
| | **Google Flights** | Fast search, price graph, “Explore” map. | Quick price trend checks and itinerary planning. |
| | **Momondo** | Price comparison, “Price Calendar”, “Price Alerts”. | Good for spotting hidden deals. |
| | **Priceline** | “Name Your Own Price” and “Express Deals” for last‑minute savings. | Bargain hunting for flexible travelers. |
| | **Travelocity** | Similar to Expedia, often bundled with hotel deals. | All‑in‑one travel package. |
| | **Orbitz** | Loyalty program (Orbucks), bundle discounts. | Frequent traveler rewards. |
| | **Hotwire** | “Hot Rate” discounted fares, “Hot Deals” for hotels. | Low‑price last‑minute bookings. |
| | **CheapOair** | Discounted fares, promo codes, “Deal of the Day”. | Budget‑focused travelers. |
| | **Booking.com** | Primarily hotels but also offers flights. | One‑stop for accommodation + flight. |
| | **Trip.com** | Global OTA, strong presence in Asia. | International travel, especially Asia. |
| | **Airfarewatchdog** | Price alerts, coupon codes, “Deal of the Day”. | Deal hunters. |
| | **Hipmunk** | “Best Time to Book” feature, “Smart Travel” algorithm. | Optimizing cost vs. convenience. |
| | **Travelzoo** | Curated travel deals, coupons. | Finding curated discounts. |
| | **Lastminute.com** | Last‑minute flight & package deals. | Impulse or flexible travelers. |
| | **Opodo** | European OTA, flight + hotel bundles. | European travel. |
| | **eDreams** | Low‑cost flights, “eDreams Deals”. | Budget travelers. |
| | **TUI** | Integrated travel agency, flights + holiday packages. | All‑inclusive holiday planning. |
| | **Travelgenio** | Global OTA, flight + hotel combos. | International travel. |
| | **Travelpayouts** | Affiliate network, flight search API. | Developers building flight search widgets. |
| | **Skiplagged** | Hidden‑city ticketing, price comparison. | Advanced fare hunting. |
| | **FlightNetwork** | Global flight search, price alerts. | General flight comparison. |
| | **FlightHub** | Low‑cost carrier aggregator. | Budget airlines. |
| | **JetRadar** | Flight search, price alerts. | Quick fare checks. |
| | **FlightAware** | Flight status tracking, real‑time flight data. | Monitoring flight progress. |

---

### How to choose the right tool

1. **Budget‑focused**  
   *Use:* Skyscanner, Google Flights, Kayak, Momondo, CheapOair, Airfarewatchdog.  
   *Why:* These sites compare many carriers and show price trends.

2. **All‑in‑one travel planning**  
   *Use:* Expedia, Travelocity, Orbitz, Booking.com, Trip.com.  
   *Why:* Bundle flights with hotels or car rentals for extra savings.

3. **Last‑minute or flexible travelers**  
   *Use:* Hotwire, Priceline Express Deals, Lastminute.com.  
   *Why:* Discounted fares for short‑notice bookings.

4. **Frequent flyer / loyalty programs**  
   *Use:* Orbitz (Orbucks), Expedia (Rewards), Priceline (Points).  
   *Why:* Earn points or miles that can be redeemed later.

5. **Advanced fare hunting**  
   *Use:* Skiplagged (hidden‑city), Hopper (predictive pricing).  
   *Why:* Find unconventional routes or future price forecasts.

6. **Flight status & operational data**  
   *Use:* FlightAware, FlightRadar24, FlightStats.  
   *Why:* Track delays, cancellations, and real‑time flight information.

---

### Quick‑start checklist

| Step | Action | Tool |
|------|--------|------|
| 1 | Search for flights | Google Flights / Skyscanner |
| 2 | Compare prices & dates | Kayak / Momondo |
| 3 | Check airline’s own site | Airline website (e.g., Delta, United) |
| 4 | Book & pay | OTA or airline site |
| 5 | Manage itinerary | Airline app / OTA app |
| 6 | Track flight status | FlightAware / FlightRadar24 |

---

### Bonus: APIs for developers

If you’re building a flight‑booking widget or integrating flight data into an app, consider these APIs:

| API | Description | Use‑case |
|-----|-------------|----------|
| **Skyscanner API** | Flight search, price alerts, multi‑city itineraries. | Build custom flight search UI. |
| **Google Flights API** (via Google Cloud) | Flight search, price history. | Data analytics, price forecasting. |
| **FlightAware API** | Real‑time flight status, historical data. | Flight tracking dashboards. |
| **OpenSky Network API** | Live flight data, ADS‑B feeds. | Aviation enthusiasts, research. |
| **Travelpayouts API** | Affiliate flight search, price comparison. | Monetize flight search widgets. |
| **Amadeus API** | Comprehensive travel data (flights, hotels, car rentals). | Enterprise travel solutions. |
| **Sabre API** | Global distribution system (GDS) for airlines. | Airline booking systems. |
| **IATA API** | Airport codes, airline data. | Data enrichment. |

---

### Final thought

The “tool” you pick depends on what matters most to you: price, convenience, flexibility, or a bundled experience. Most travelers start with a comparison engine (Google Flights, Skyscanner, Kayak) and then book directly through the airline or an OTA that offers the best deal or loyalty benefits. Happy travels!
